metadata.name: H2/2 level, frozen, SLOW prior · state_prior_lr 0.02 (was 0.1: a 200 ms step against a 200 ms actuator lag chased the gait to the rails)
metadata.description: The head loop on TWO motors — head_pitch and head_roll — with neck_pitch and head_yaw held at zero (2026-09-10, after H2 on four motors wound every command to its rail: the two pitch joints are a redundant pair whose null space, neck up + head down, the sensor cannot see, and the prior's bias drifted into it). Load slots as head_h1: roll, pitch, down-shortfall | head gyro x,y,z | trunk gravity x,y | trunk gyro x,y,z | spare; with motor_dim 2 the load rows start at 6, so the level prior is state_prior_indices [6, 7]. H2: babble 0, state_prior on load slots 6,7 (roll, pitch) -> 0, gain 1, lr 0.1. model_lr 0 and state_model_lr 0: the model stays as H1 identified it on a still body; the module's own note warns that the closed-loop model after a babble can bear no resemblance to the babbled one, and the prior acts through whatever the model says. state_prior_lr 0.02: the Gauss-Newton step per tick is a fifth of the model-implied correction (a ~1 s time constant) instead of a tenth at 50 Hz (~200 ms, the walker's head lag) — the operator saw the head level fore-aft like a bird and the roll bang between its rails in turns; the roll and pitch commands sat at their rails on half the ticks.
